requirements.quote:
A Retry packet causes a client to send another Initial packet,
   effectively restarting the connection process.
requirements.condition: When a client processes a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Send another Initial packet, thereby restarting the connection process.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue the connection attempt without sending another Initial packet.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a Retry packet and verify that the client's next connection-starting transmission includes another Initial packet.

requirements.quote:
A Retry packet
   indicates that the Initial packet was received but not processed.
requirements.condition: When a client interprets a Retry packet in relation to its preceding Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the preceding Initial packet as received by the server but not processed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Infer from the Retry packet that the preceding Initial packet was processed.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: Client state and subsequent recovery behavior can be inspected to determine whether the preceding Initial is marked as processed.

requirements.quote:
A
   Retry packet cannot be treated as an acknowledgment because it does
   not indicate that a packet was processed or specify the packet
   number.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Process the Retry packet without treating it as an acknowledgment of any packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the Retry packet as acknowledgment evidence, mark a packet acknowledged, or associate it with an acknowledged packet number.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused test can compare acknowledgment, in-flight, and loss-recovery state before and after receipt of a Retry packet.

requirements.quote:
Clients that receive a Retry packet reset congestion control and loss
   recovery state, including resetting any pending timers.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Carry congestion-control state from before the Retry into the restarted connection process.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: Congestion-control variables can be seeded before Retry processing and inspected afterward for reinitialization.

requirements.quote:
Clients that receive a Retry packet reset congestion control and loss
   recovery state, including resetting any pending timers.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Carry loss-recovery state from before the Retry into the restarted connection process.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: Loss-recovery variables can be seeded before Retry processing and inspected afterward for reinitialization.

requirements.quote:
Clients that receive a Retry packet reset congestion control and loss
   recovery state, including resetting any pending timers.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a Retry packet while congestion-control or loss-recovery timers are pending.
requirements.required_behavior: Reset all pending timers that belong to congestion-control or loss-recovery state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leave a pre-Retry congestion-control or loss-recovery timer pending with its old deadline or state.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can arm recovery timers, deliver Retry, and inspect timer cancellation or reinitialization and subsequent firing behavior.

requirements.quote:
Other
   connection state, in particular cryptographic handshake messages, is
   retained; see Section 17.2.5 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
requirements.condition: When a client resets congestion-control and loss-recovery state after receiving a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Retain connection state outside congestion-control and loss-recovery state, including cryptographic handshake messages.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discard cryptographic handshake messages or other unaffected connection state solely because a Retry packet was received.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is prescribed.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection and handshake state can be populated before Retry processing and checked afterward for preservation.

requirements.quote:
The client MAY compute an RTT estimate to the server as the time
   period from when the first Initial packet was sent to when a Retry or
   a Version Negotiation packet is received.
requirements.condition: When a client chooses to compute an RTT estimate from receipt of a Retry or Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.required_behavior: It may compute the estimate as the elapsed time from sending the first Initial packet to receiving the Retry or Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat this optional computation as mandatory.
requirements.error_behavior: No error is required when the client does not exercise this option.
requirements.why_checkable: If the option is implemented, controlled send and receive timestamps can verify the estimate's start and end events; omission of the option is also permitted.

requirements.quote:
The client MAY use this
   value in place of its default for the initial RTT estimate.
requirements.condition: When the client has computed the RTT value described from the first Initial and a received Retry or Version Negotiation packet.
requirements.required_behavior: It may substitute that computed value for the default initial RTT estimate.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat substitution of the computed value as mandatory.
requirements.error_behavior: No error is required when the client retains its default initial RTT estimate.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial RTT value used by loss recovery can be observed after supplying a controlled elapsed interval, while retaining the default remains conformant.
